notes.meaning: God gave a direct message to Ezekiel. The prophet did not invent these warnings, but faithfully spoke what the Lord told him. God spoke to guide His people during a time of great confusion.

God told Ezekiel to speak against the people in Israel who pretended to be prophets. These men were not sent by God, but made up messages from their own wishes and imagination. They told the people what they wanted to hear instead of God's real truth.

God pronounced sorrow on these foolish prophets. Real wisdom begins with fearing God, but these men followed their own feelings and never saw a true vision from heaven. They claimed to know God's mind while having no real relationship with Him.

The false prophets were like hungry foxes scurrying through ruins. Instead of guarding the nation like a faithful watchman, they used the people's troubles for their own selfish gain. They cared only about feeding themselves and tore down what little was left.

When an enemy attacked a city, brave soldiers rushed to the broken gaps in the wall to defend it. Faithful prophets were supposed to defend the people by praying and calling them to turn from their sins. These false prophets did nothing to stop the nation's spiritual collapse or prepare them for God's judgment.

These deceivers told lies and claimed the Lord sent them, even though He never did. Worse still, after convincing the people, they actually fooled themselves into hoping their predictions would come true. Believing your own lies does not make them true in God's eyes.

God challenged these prophets directly about their empty claims. They boldly claimed to speak in God's name, even though He had stayed completely silent. Using the name of the Lord to push personal opinions is a grave offense to Him.

Because these prophets spread empty words and fake visions, the Lord announced that He stood against them. Prophets should have enjoyed God's blessing and favor, but these men turned Him into their enemy. No one can stand secure when God is opposing their work.

God promised to remove these false prophets through three clear losses. They would lose their seats among the respected leaders, their names would be left off the official citizen lists of Israel, and they would never return to the promised land. Their rejection showed that pretending to serve God will end in total loss.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Some Catholic commentary notes that these men would lose their influence as advisers, and their writings would never be accepted as holy Scripture.

notes.meaning: The prophets misled the people by promising peace when destruction was right at the door. One prophet made up an imaginary plan of safety like a flimsy wall, and the others smeared whitewash over it to hide the cracks. Covering over deep sin with cheap flattery never brings real safety.

God commanded Ezekiel to tell these builders that their painted wall would crash down. A fierce storm of pouring rain, falling hailstones, and powerful winds would tear through it. This storm pictured the Babylonian army that God was sending to destroy their false hopes.

When the wall collapsed into rubble, people would mock the prophets who had painted over the cracks. Everyone would ask where all their fine whitewash went. A lie may look attractive for a short time, but real trouble will show how useless it is.

The Lord declared that He was the one bringing this destructive storm in His anger. The wind, rain, and hailstones were tools of His holy wrath against stubborn unfaithfulness. The coming disaster was not an accident, but God's own righteous judgment.

God promised to smash the plastered wall completely flat so that its very foundations would be exposed. When the city fell, the lying prophets who gave bad advice would die right inside it. That terrible fall would prove to everyone that the Lord's warnings were true.

God would finish His wrath against both the weak wall and the men who covered it in plaster. When the dust cleared, the Lord would announce that the fake defense and its builders were completely gone. Relying on made-up hopes leaves people with nothing in the end.

These plasterers were the very prophets who told Jerusalem that everything would turn out fine. They claimed to see peace, but there was no peace for a nation living in rebellion against God. True peace only comes when people turn back to the Lord in sincerity.

Ezekiel was told to stand firm and speak out against women who were making up prophecies out of their own hearts. God had spoken through godly women like Deborah and Huldah in the past, but these women were running selfish frauds. God holds everyone accountable when they twist His truth.

These women sewed cushions for people's arms and made special veils for heads of every size as superstitious rituals. They used these objects to promise comfort and victory, trapping simple people like prey in a net. They tried to gain wealth and influence by keeping others spiritually blind.

These women dragged God's name into the mud just to earn tiny handouts of barley and bread. They used lies to terrify faithful people who should have lived in hope, and promised life to wicked people who deserved death. Selling spiritual truth for cheap material gain is a terrible sin.

God announced that He was totally against their magical charms and trickery. He promised to rip those bands from their arms and set free the trapped people, just like a hunter's net releasing captured birds. The Lord cares for His people and breaks the power of deceitful traps.

God also promised to tear away their magic veils and rescue His people completely from their grip. The deceivers would no longer treat God's flock like prey. When God rescues His people from false teachers, everyone sees His true power and mercy.

These women brought deep sorrow to the hearts of the righteous by threatening them with lies that God never spoke. At the same time, they encouraged the wicked to keep on sinning by falsely promising them safety and life. A message that discourages the good and comforts the rebellious does not come from God.

Because of their harmful work, God would put an absolute stop to their false visions and fortune-telling. He would free His people from their control and expose their fraud before everyone. When God steps in, all false teachings are silenced and the Lord is known as the true King.
